item.title: Toyota Commemorative Museum: From Looms to Cars — Guide
item.description: The Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology occupies the handsome red-brick spinning mill that Sakichi Toyoda founded in Nagoya in 1911, and it tells one of Japan’s great industrial stories: how a maker of automatic textile looms transformed itself into the world’s largest carmaker. The textile pavilion sets dozens of historic looms clattering in live demonstrations, from hand spinning to the revolutionary Type G automatic loom, while the automobile pavilion walks through car development and production with cutaway engines, robots and demonstrations that make manufacturing genuinely fascinating even for visitors who never thought they cared.
